subject: Paynetic Dedicated pool: urgent throughput & 5xx increase
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan@paynetic.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in latency and 5xx on our dedicated pool (Paynetic)

Chloe —

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and median latency has jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s starting ~07:50 PDT. This is hitting our production payment scoring endpoint hard and causing transaction retries. Our engineers see sustained CPU/GPU saturation in the Paynetic dedicated pool and several requests are queuing.

Attached is the first slice of logs (we'll forward more if useful). Can you confirm this is isolated to our reserved capacity or if it's a cross-tenant issue? We are on a reserved commit and need immediate mitigation — business impact is rising fast.

Evan
Evan Liu
Senior Engineering Manager, Paynetic
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan@paynetic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -07:00

Evan — thanks for the alert and the logs. I'm investigating now. Quick notes:
- I'm looping in Ben (acct lead) and Marissa (CS) so they can coordinate account communications.
- Dylan, can you pull the pool metrics / queue depths and confirm whether autoscale / burst is being blocked by reservation ceiling?

Planned immediate actions:
1) Dylan to provide short diagnostic (10m).
2) If reserved throughput is saturated, request emergency burst authorization and route to cross-region fallback while we stabilize.
3) We'll share a crisp timeline with Paynetic in 30 minutes.

I'll keep you updated in-thread.

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in latency and 5xx on our dedicated pool (Paynetic)

Quick diagnostic (first 10m):
- Observed: sustained GPU utilization at 98-100% across Paynetic's dedicated nodes, KV-cache miss rate up ~4x vs baseline, request queue depth spiking to 2.2k.
- Error profile: ~85% of 5xx are timeout/queue-exhaustion from inference runtime (not upstream code). Some tail OOM retries present but minor.
- Autoscale: blocked — reservation policy prevents adding host capacity above the committed pool without a burst authorization.

Immediate mitigations I can run now (need approval):
A) Trigger emergency burst (spin up +20% capacity) — requires Sales/Finance approval and will apply a temporary overage charge as per contract. I have a prepared request doc (request_burst_doc.pdf).
B) Force route a subset of traffic to cross-region fallback (latency tradeoff) for highest-traffic routes — quick to enact but will increase token cost + latency ~120-180ms.
C) Flush KV prefix caches for the longest-blocking models (short-term latency improvement, risk: cold-cache cold starts).

I recommend B+C immediately while we await authorization for A. I can execute B+C in ~8 minutes once you give the go-ahead. Logs attached: paynetic_error_log_20270824.txt (tail).

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan@paynetic.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in latency and 5xx on our dedicated pool (Paynetic)

Evan — 

Thanks for the logs and flagging this. We own this with you and apologize for the impact. We're proposing a two-step plan:
1) Short-term: route the top 3 application routes to our cross-region fallback and flush the largest KV prefixes (Chloe/Dylan will run this). This should reduce 5xx and bring median latency back under 400ms within 10-20 minutes.
2) Mid-term: we will request an emergency +20% burst for Paynetic's dedicated pool. I've attached the request document; please confirm you approve Redwood initiating the burst and acknowledge the temporary overage charge. We will seek finance sign-off immediately.

If you want us to sign a temporary credit to offset costs, we can discuss — I will also escalate for leadership approval. Please reply OK to proceed with the short-term steps.

—Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0189
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec heads-up: Paynetic reserved-capacity saturation + customer impact (urgent)

Jonas — looping you in because Paynetic is a high-priority reserved customer (DN-47821) and this event is causing revenue-impacting transaction errors. Summary and asks: 

Summary:
- At ~07:50 PDT Paynetic's dedicated GPU pool hit sustained 98-100% utilization; queue depths exceeded policy thresholds and the runtime returned elevated 5xx (timeouts / queue exhaustion).
- Short-term mitigations (executed): cross-region fallback routing for top routes + KV flushes — customer reports error rate falling but still above SLO (working to ~1.1% 5xx down from 5.6%).
- Remaining risk: customer sees elevated latency and repeat retries; reserved throughput ceiling prevented immediate autoscale.

Asks / proposed decisions:
1) Authorization to approve emergency +20% burst for Paynetic (A) — this will reduce queueing rapidly. Finance will need to accept overage. Ben can action customer approval; I request your sign-off to fast-track our internal finance approval.
2) Short postmortem and rollout of a plan to avoid reservation-blocking for business-critical routes (policy change proposal to allow emergency temporary headroom for top-tier reserved customers). I'll draft the policy and bring to you for review.
3) If you prefer, offer Paynetic a one-time credit to offset the burst charge — ok for me to discuss with Finance and CS, but would appreciate a quick greenlight.

Context: Paynetic handles live payments for several merchants; sustained outages >15m materially affect revenue and retention. We have a DocuSign ready if a commercial concession is required.

I'll keep you posted on the regen of 5xx. Current status: customer-visible errors trending down, but we still need capacity relief to normalize tail latency.

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
